## Professional career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmer_Fredette&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Professional career")]

### Sacramento Kings (2011–2014)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmer_Fredette&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Sacramento Kings (2011–2014)")]

On June 23, 2011, Fredette was selected by the [Milwaukee Bucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee_Bucks "Milwaukee Bucks") with the 10th overall pick in the [2011 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_NBA_draft "2011 NBA draft"). He was subsequently traded to the [Sacramento Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacramento_Kings "Sacramento Kings") in a deal with Milwaukee and the [Charlotte Bobcats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte_Bobcats "Charlotte Bobcats") involving [John Salmons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Salmons "John Salmons"), [Beno Udrih](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beno_Udrih "Beno Udrih"), [Shaun Livingston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaun_Livingston "Shaun Livingston"), [Corey Maggette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corey_Maggette "Corey Maggette"), and [Stephen Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Jackson "Stephen Jackson").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-41)

"Jimmermania" in Sacramento was felt immediately as he recharged the fan base. Sales of his jersey resulted in a 540% increase in [Sacramento Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacramento_Kings "Sacramento Kings") merchandise sales, as his No. 7 Kings jersey sold out in stores in the Sacramento area, as well as online.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-42) Fredette made his rookie debut in a preseason game against the [Golden State Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_State_Warriors "Golden State Warriors") on December 17, 2011, scoring 21 points (tied for team high) and recording 4 rebounds.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-44) He got his first start on January 10, 2012, against the [Philadelphia 76ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_76ers "Philadelphia 76ers").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-45)

On February 12, 2014, Fredette scored a career-high 24 points, along with two assists and six three-pointers, in a 106–101 overtime win over the [New York Knicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Knicks "New York Knicks").[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-46) On February 27, 2014, Fredette's contract was bought out by the Kings.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-47)

### Chicago Bulls (2014)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmer_Fredette&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Chicago Bulls (2014)")]

On March 2, 2014, Fredette signed with the [Chicago Bulls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bulls "Chicago Bulls") for the rest of the 2013–14 season.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-48)

### New Orleans Pelicans (2014–2015)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmer_Fredette&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: New Orleans Pelicans (2014–2015)")]

On July 24, 2014, Fredette signed with the [New Orleans Pelicans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans_Pelicans "New Orleans Pelicans").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-49) On December 31, 2014, he had a season-best game with 14 points and 3 rebounds in a 95–93 overtime loss to the [San Antonio Spurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Antonio_Spurs "San Antonio Spurs").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-50)

On July 22, 2015, Fredette signed with the Spurs.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-51) However, he was later waived by the Spurs on October 21, 2015, after appearing in two preseason games.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-52) On October 31, Fredette was selected by the [Westchester Knicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westchester_Knicks "Westchester Knicks") with the second overall pick in the 2015 [NBA Development League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Development_League "NBA Development League") Draft.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-53)

On November 10, 2015, Fredette re-signed with the Pelicans to help the team deal with numerous injuries. New Orleans had to use an NBA hardship exception in order to sign him as he made their roster stand at 16, one over the allowed limit of 15.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-54) On November 19, he was waived by the Pelicans.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-55)

### Westchester Knicks (2015–2016)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmer_Fredette&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Westchester Knicks (2015–2016)")]

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/41/Jimmer_Fredette_with_Westchester.JPG/250px-Jimmer_Fredette_with_Westchester.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jimmer_Fredette_with_Westchester.JPG)

Fredette with Westchester in 2016

On November 28, 2015, Fredette was reacquired by the Westchester Knicks.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-56) He made his debut for the Knicks two days later, recording 37 points and eight assists in a 102–90 win over the [Grand Rapids Drive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Rapids_Drive "Grand Rapids Drive").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-57) On January 29, 2016, he was named to the East All-Star team for the 2016 [NBA D-League All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Development_League_All-Star_Game "NBA Development League All-Star Game").[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-58) On February 13, he led the East All-Star team to a 128–124 win over the West, winning the D-League All-Star Game MVP trophy after recording 35 points, six rebounds, eight assists, and one steal in 25 minutes.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-59)

### New York Knicks (2016)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmer_Fredette&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: New York Knicks (2016)")]

On February 22, 2016, Fredette signed a ten-day contract with the [New York Knicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Knicks "New York Knicks").[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-60) That night he made his debut for New York in a 122–95 loss to the [Toronto Raptors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_Raptors "Toronto Raptors"), recording three points in two minutes off the bench.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-61) On March 2, the Knicks chose not to offer Fredette a second 10-day contract, making him a free agent.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-62)

### Return to Westchester (2016)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmer_Fredette&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Return to Westchester (2016)")]

On March 6, Fredette was reacquired by Westchester.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-63) At the season's end, he was named to the [All-NBA D-League Second Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-NBA_Development_League_Team "All-NBA Development League Team").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-64) Fredette played for the [Denver Nuggets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Nuggets "Denver Nuggets") Summer League team during the 2016 NBA offseason, but was not signed by an NBA team.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-deseret.com-65)

### Shanghai Sharks (2016–2019)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmer_Fredette&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Shanghai Sharks (2016–2019)")]

On August 2, 2016, Fredette signed with the [Shanghai Sharks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_Sharks "Shanghai Sharks") of the [Chinese Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Basketball_Association "Chinese Basketball Association") (CBA).[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-66) Early in the season, on November 11, he had a 51-point outing against the [Guangdong Southern Tigers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangdong_Southern_Tigers "Guangdong Southern Tigers").[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-67) On February 19, 2017, Fredette scored 73 points in Shanghai's 135–132 [double overtime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_(sports) "Overtime (sports)") loss to [Zhejiang Guangsha Lions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_Guangsha_Lions "Zhejiang Guangsha Lions").[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-68) He was subsequently named the CBA's [International Regular Season MVP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBA_International_Most_Valuable_Player "CBA International Most Valuable Player") of the [2016–17 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_CBA_season "2016–17 CBA season").[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-69) In 41 games, he averaged 37.6 points, 8.2 rebounds, 4.2 assists, and 1.6 steals per game. He shot 52.5% from the field on 2-point field goal attempts, 47.4% from the field, 39.6% from 3-point range, and 93.3% from the free throw line.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-70) He ranked first in the CBA in points per game scoring average, over all phases of the season;[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-auto-71) and he ranked second in the league in scoring, during the first phase of the season, which determines [the league's scoring champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Basketball_Association_scoring_leaders "Chinese Basketball Association scoring leaders").[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-72)

On July 23, 2017, Fredette re-signed with the Sharks on a two-year deal.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-73)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-74) On November 11, Fredette recorded a career-high 75 points (including him scoring a record-high 40 in the fourth quarter) in a 137–136 loss to the [Beikong Fly Dragons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beikong_Fly_Dragons "Beikong Fly Dragons").[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-75) At the end of the [2018–19 CBA season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_CBA_season "2018–19 CBA season"), he led the entire league in overall total points scored, however [Pierre Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_Jackson "Pierre Jackson") was the [league's scoring champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Basketball_Association_scoring_leaders "Chinese Basketball Association scoring leaders"), as he led the league in points per game.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-76)

### Phoenix Suns (2019)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmer_Fredette&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Phoenix Suns (2019)")]

On March 22, 2019, Fredette signed a two-year contract with the [Phoenix Suns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix_Suns "Phoenix Suns").[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-77) He made his official return to the NBA a day later against his first NBA team, the [Sacramento Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacramento_Kings "Sacramento Kings").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-78) In his next game on March 25, Fredette was given a standing ovation in his return to Utah in a loss against the [Utah Jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah_Jazz "Utah Jazz").[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-79) However, after only playing in six games and averaging only 3.7 points per game, on June 24, Phoenix declined to pick up the second-year option of Fredette's deal[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-80) and his short return to the NBA ended. He would be the last Sun to wear #32 before it was retired in honor of [Amar'e Stoudemire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amar'e_Stoudemire "Amar'e Stoudemire").

### Panathinaikos (2019–2020)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmer_Fredette&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Panathinaikos (2019–2020)")]

On July 15, 2019, Fredette signed a two-year contract with [Panathinaikos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panathinaikos_B.C. "Panathinaikos B.C.") of Greece's [top-tier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_basketball_league_system "Greek basketball league system") level [Greek Basketball League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_Basketball_League "Greek Basketball League") and the [EuroLeague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EuroLeague "EuroLeague").[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-81) When the Greek League suspended play due to the COVID-19 pandemic, Panathinaikos was named league champion.

Panathinaikos experienced serious financial difficulties as a result of the pandemic, and on July 4, 2020, the team announced that Fredette's contract was too heavy for the team's budget. As a result, Fredette was essentially laid off.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-82)

### Return to Shanghai (2020–2021)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmer_Fredette&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Return to Shanghai (2020–2021)")]

On September 6, Fredette confirmed via Twitter that he intended to return to the [Shanghai Sharks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_Sharks "Shanghai Sharks"), and he made his return debut on October 18.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-83) On October 20, he scored 26 points to lead all scorers as the Sharks earned their first win of the season, 95–88 over the Shanxi Sturgeons.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-84) Fredette became the Shanghai Sharks all time 3-point leader on December 29, 2020.

As a result of the pandemic, Fredette was forced to leave China early in 2021 and suspend his involvement with the Shanghai Sharks. On August 5, 2021, as it became clear that foreign players likely would not be able to compete in the 2021–22 CBA season, Fredette was signed to the [Denver Nuggets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Nuggets "Denver Nuggets") Summer League roster for the second time.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-deseret.com-65) However, he almost immediately withdrew from Summer League play due to unspecified issues.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-85)

### The Basketball Tournament

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmer_Fredette&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: The Basketball Tournament")]

Fredette has participated in [The Basketball Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Basketball_Tournament "The Basketball Tournament") (TBT), a million-dollar winner-take-all summer tournament broadcast on the [ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPN "ESPN") family of channels. In [TBT 2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Basketball_Tournament_2017 "The Basketball Tournament 2017"), he acted as coach for Team Fredette,[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-86) which lost in the first round to Team Utah, 100–97. In [TBT 2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Basketball_Tournament_2018 "The Basketball Tournament 2018"), he played for Team Fredette,[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-87) leading the team to four wins and a spot in the semifinals, where they lost to [Eberlein Drive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eberlein_Drive "Eberlein Drive"), 80–76.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-88) He returned as a player in [TBT 2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Basketball_Tournament_2022 "The Basketball Tournament 2022"), with The Money Team.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-89)

### 3x3 basketball and Olympics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmer_Fredette&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: 3x3 basketball and Olympics")]

In 2022, Fredette made his 3x3 debut at the 2022 Red Bull USA Basketball 3X East Regional, which took place October 8–9 in New York, and helped team NYC Blue win the event. On October 25, 2022, Fredette, [Canyon Barry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canyon_Barry "Canyon Barry"), [Kareem Maddox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kareem_Maddox "Kareem Maddox"), and Dylan Travis were named to the USA Men's 2022 3x3 AmeriCup team.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-90) At the 2022 FIBA 3x3 AmeriCup, which took place November 4–6 in Miami, Fredette and his team won gold.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-91) In FIBA 3x3 World Cup 2023, Fredette played for USA, winning the silver medal,[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-92) and Fredette was selected for the Team of the Tournament.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-93)

In 2024, Fredette represented [Team USA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_at_the_Olympics "United States at the Olympics") at the [2024 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics "2024 Summer Olympics") as a member of the first [USA Basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Basketball "USA Basketball") 3x3 Men's National Team to compete at the Olympics.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-94)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-95) Fredette suffered an adductor tear in the second pool play game and didn't play in four of the games, and the team was eliminated after going 2–5.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-96)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-97)

On April 23, 2025, Fredette announced his retirement from basketball.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-98)

## Playing style and personality

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmer_Fredette&action=edit&section=30 "Edit section: Playing style and personality")]

In a January 2011 article, _[Sports Illustrated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports\_Illustrated "Sports Illustrated")_ writer Kelli Anderson said about Fredette's playing style:

> Facing the opposition's best defender (or, more often, defenders), he pulls up going right or going left. He shoots off the dribble, off the wrong foot, off balance, off the glass. He finishes in traffic with a dozen deft moves, including a scoop shot, originating from his waist, that he can make with either hand.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-Anderson1-100)

His skills were noted by several collegiate and NBA players across the country. [Kevin Durant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Durant "Kevin Durant") of the [Oklahoma City Thunder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma_City_Thunder "Oklahoma City Thunder") posted on his Twitter account that "Jimmer Fredette is the best scorer in the world!",[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-101) while [Steve Nash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Nash "Steve Nash") of the [Phoenix Suns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix_Suns "Phoenix Suns") tweeted "Jimmer Fredette? That name's straight out of Hoosiers. No wonder he never misses."[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-102)[Jared Sullinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jared_Sullinger "Jared Sullinger"), a forward at [Ohio State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_State_University "Ohio State University"), said "Jimmer is going off right now. Pure scorer."[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-103)

Other facets of his personality were noted by other college coaches. Former [Utah Utes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah_Utes "Utah Utes") coach [Jim Boylen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Boylen "Jim Boylen") cited "swagger and confidence" as Fredette's biggest weapons, and [Villanova's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villanova_Wildcats_men's_basketball "Villanova Wildcats men's basketball")[Jay Wright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Wright_(coach) "Jay Wright (coach)") also remarked favorably on Fredette's on-court aggressiveness, comparing him to [Pete Maravich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_Maravich "Pete Maravich") in that respect. However, Kelli Anderson described Fredette as "fiercely competitive while remaining unassuming and likable," noting that [Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_Wildcats_men's_basketball "Arizona Wildcats men's basketball") coach [Sean Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Miller "Sean Miller") hugged Fredette after he scored 49 on the Wildcats.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-Anderson1-100)

Fredette describes his older brother TJ as his biggest fan and supporter. TJ, a rapper whose song "Amazing" was written for his brother, said, "I see him play, and it gives me chills sometimes when he hits some of those big shots and the crowd is going crazy."[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-104)

In an article published in _Sports Illustrated_, [Marcus Morris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcus_Morris_(basketball) "Marcus Morris (basketball)"), a forward at Kansas, noted the work ethic and moral character Fredette exhibited while at USA Basketball camp. He said, "He's got heart. You can see he has a feel for the game, and he can shoot it from anywhere. Even if you try to box-and-one the guy, he brings it up and just pulls up from the hashmark. That's tough to guard."[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-TourneySI-37)

An unusual set of Fredette fans resided in the [Mount McGregor Correctional Facility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_McGregor_Correctional_Facility "Mount McGregor Correctional Facility"), a medium-security prison, where he and his older brother played games with the inmates. Fredette credits these experiences as helping with his focus in rough situations. The prison closed in 2014.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-105)[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-106)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-107)

Upon entering the NBA, Fredette struggled to find his game, with Yahoo Sports' Michael Lee noting that Fredette's inability to adjust from being a scorer to more of a role player could ultimately usher an end to his career.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-108)

After signing with the CBA's [Shanghai Sharks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_Sharks "Shanghai Sharks"), Fredette became a dominant player in the Chinese Basketball League, leading his team to the playoffs in 3 of his 4 years there. He also acquired the fan nickname "Jimo Dashen", which translates to "The Lonely Master" or "The Lonely God" in Chinese. Fredette commented on this during an interview: "It's not necessarily the same sense that you think about being lonely. In America, you just think you are by yourself and depressed and that type of stuff. But in this way, it more means that you're on top, and nobody is around you."[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-109)

Fredette became a leader on his team, although, particularly early in his CBA career, his primary form of communication with his teammates was via an interpreter.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-110)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmer_Fredette&action=edit&section=31 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Fredette is married to Whitney Wonnacott and the couple has three children. Fredette met his wife while at BYU where she was a cheerleader,[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-111) and the two were married in 2012 in the [Denver Colorado Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Colorado_Temple "Denver Colorado Temple").[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-112)[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-113) During the 2017 CBA playoffs, Fredette missed his team's first playoff game because he traveled home to [Denver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver "Denver") to be with his wife during the birth of their first child.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette#cite_note-114)
